title: Bridge deterioration in the US National Bridge Inventory
summary: Bridges are built in cohorts, wear with age and are repaired or replaced; inspections rate their components 0-9, and the lowest rating sets good, fair or poor. One inventory shows the stock's ages, not one bridge's life.

concepts.label: Highway bridge
concepts.description: A structure over 20 ft (6.1 m) carrying a public road, one NBI record.

facts.text: The NBI covers over 620,000 bridges on public roads; this copy is as of June 20, 2025.

children.label: Construction cohort
children.description: Bridges built in the same span: the 1956-1980 interstate era is a third of the stock.

children.label: Main-span material
children.description: NBI item 43A: concrete, steel, prestressed concrete, timber, masonry, iron.

children.label: Reconstruction
children.description: NBI item 106: the year of the latest major reconstruction.

children.label: Traffic load
children.description: Average daily traffic (item 29) and truck share (item 109): the loads that fatigue decks.

concepts.label: Condition rating
concepts.description: 0-9 inspector ratings of deck, superstructure, substructure (items 58-60) and culvert (62); the lowest decides the class: good ≥ 7, fair 5-6, poor ≤ 4.

facts.text: Coding Guide for the Structure Inventory and Appraisal of the Nation's Bridges.

children.label: Wear-in rate
children.description: Growth of ln(poor share) per year of age; its doubling time.

children.label: Markov deterioration model
children.description: Ratings as states with yearly transition probabilities (as in AASHTOWare BrM); needs ratings followed year by year.

children.label: Element-level condition
children.description: Condition states per element (bearings, joints, girders) from the newer SNBI/element data.

concepts.label: Bridge stock projection
concepts.description: Each cohort aged 10 or 20 years at today's age-specific poor shares: the demographic momentum of the inventory.

children.label: Survivor bias
children.description: Old cohorts hold the bridges that were not replaced, so a cross-section flattens the deterioration curve.

children.label: Design life
children.description: 50 years in older AASHTO practice, 75 years in LRFD (since 1994).
